Operator: Good day, and welcome to the SecureNet Q2 Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Lisa Grant, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Lisa Grant: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss SecureNet's results for the second quarter fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Alex Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Priya Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Lisa, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. SecureNet had a strong second quarter, driven by continued demand for our cybersecurity solutions and our commitment to innovation. We are seeing increased adoption of our SecureXDR platform, which is helping organizations better protect themselves against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

Our focus remains on four key areas: navigating the evolving threat landscape, scaling new customer acquisitions, leveraging strong customer feedback on our new products and features, and growing average deal sizes for both new and existing customers.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Mark. As Mark mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $295 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. This growth was driven by strong performance across all of our product lines, including 42% year-over-year ARR growth and a record $2.3 billion in total backlog entering Q3. Our gross margin was 82%, and our operating expenses were $180 million. Net income for the quarter was $75 million, or $1.05 per diluted share.

We are confident that we are well-positioned to continue to drive growth and profitability in the years to come.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the question and answer session. First question comes from John Smith with Morgan Stanley.

John Smith: Thanks, and good afternoon, team. Congrats on another solid quarter. Could you provide more details on the number of new customers you acquired this quarter, including any breakdowns by segment and region?

Mark Thompson: Thanks, John, and thanks to everyone on the call for joining us today. Absolutely happy to dive deep into new customer acquisitions, one of our key growth metrics. In Q2 fiscal 2024, we added 452 new customers, marking a robust 25% quarter-over-quarter increase from the 361 new logos we secured in Q1, and an impressive 41% year-over-year growth compared to 320 in Q2 fiscal 2023. This performance underscores the accelerating demand for our next-gen cybersecurity platform amid escalating global threats, including the recent surge in ransomware-as-a-service campaigns like LockBit 3.0 variants and the ongoing exploitation of vulnerabilities in supply chain ecosystems, reminiscent of the SolarWinds breach.

To give you a granular breakdown by customer segment, which is critical in our industry where dollar-based net expansion and retention drive long-term value: For enterprise customers, those with ARR exceeding $1 million, we onboarded 52 new enterprises, up 30% quarter-over-quarter and 44% year-over-year. Key wins included three Fortune 500 financial institutions adopting our full XDR stack—integrating our AI-native Endpoint Detection and Response, Cloud Workload Protection Platform, and Cloud Security Posture Management—to achieve Zero Trust Architecture compliance under NIST 800-207 frameworks. These deals averaged $2.8 million in initial ACV, reflecting our penetration into regulated sectors hungry for unified threat visibility post high-profile incidents like the Change Healthcare ransomware disruption.

In the mid-market segment, ARR between $100K and $1M, we added 198 new customers, representing a 28% quarter-over-quarter ramp, fueled by our SecureAccess SASE platform. Mid-markets are rapidly consolidating point solutions, and our single-pane-of-glass dashboard with ML-powered behavioral analytics has resonated strongly, displacing legacy players like legacy Check Point firewalls in 40% of these wins.

For SMBs, ARR under $100K, we brought on 202 new logos, a 20% quarter-over-quarter increase, driven by channel partnerships with over 1,200 MSSPs and VARs. Our lightweight Managed Detection and Response service, priced accessibly at $5 per endpoint per month, has lowered barriers to entry, capturing SMBs navigating the post-Log4j vulnerability landscape without in-house SOC capabilities.

Regionally, our expansion remains balanced but with clear momentum: North America had 278 new customers, 61% of the total, up 35% year-over-year; EMEA 107, 24%, up 55%; APAC 54, 12%, up 40%; and LATAM/other 13, 3%, up 160%.

North America continues to dominate, bolstered by hyperscaler integrations—our native AWS Marketplace and Azure Sentinel connector drove 35% of NA wins. EMEA's outsized growth stems from GDPR enforcement waves and sovereign data residency mandates; we closed deals with two major European telcos for our Data Loss Prevention module compliant with Schrems II. In APAC, regulatory tailwinds like Singapore's Cybersecurity Act and Australia's Essential Eight have accelerated adoption, with notable traction in Japan for our OT/IoT security extensions amid rising ICS-targeted attacks. LATAM is nascent but exploding, thanks to our first-mover partnership with Claro in Brazil for SMB MDR.

Strategically, these results reflect three technical and go-to-market initiatives we're doubling down on. First, our AI/ML innovation pipeline: The Q1 launch of our ApexAI XDR engine, leveraging generative AI for autonomous threat hunting and reducing mean-time-to-respond by 65% in beta trials, converted 28% of our proof-of-concept pipeline into wins. This positions us competitively against CrowdStrike's Falcon platform and Palo Alto's Cortex XDR, with early indicators of 140%+ net revenue retention from these cohorts.

Second, ecosystem expansion: Strategic alliances with Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange and Okta's identity fabric have unlocked co-sell opportunities, contributing to 22% of new logos. We're also piloting integrations with ServiceNow for SecOps orchestration, targeting IT service desk convergence.

Third, vertical-specific plays: In response to sector-specific threats—like the 300% year-over-year rise in healthcare breaches per Verizon's DBIR—we tailored our platform for HIPAA and HITRUST, landing five major providers. Similarly, our Critical Infrastructure Module for Purdue Model Level 3/4 OT convergence addressed CISA advisories on ransomware targeting manufacturing PLCs.

Looking forward, our Q3 pipeline stands at $1.2 billion—up 32% year-over-year—with a 42% win rate in late-stage opportunities. We expect new customer adds to accelerate to 500+ in Q3, supported by $150 million in remaining performance obligations growth from multi-year contracts. This momentum, combined with our industry-leading 125% dollar-based net revenue retention, positions SecureNet to capture share in a $200 billion+ total addressable market expanding at 12-15% CAGR, per Gartner and IDC forecasts.

John, does that cover it, or would you like more on any segment?

Operator: Thank you. Next question comes from Sarah Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Chen: Thanks, and good afternoon, team. Strong quarter—congrats on the 28% YoY revenue growth. Could you provide some color on the evolving threat landscape and how it's impacting your go-to-market strategy?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Sarah, and thanks to everyone on the call for joining us today. Absolutely, happy to dive into the threat landscape—it's the North Star guiding our R&D investments and customer conversations. We've seen an acceleration in sophistication and volume that's directly fueling our 42% ARR growth in our XDR platform and a record $2.3 billion in total backlog entering Q4.

Let me start with the macro picture. According to our internal threat intelligence fused from over 15 petabytes of telemetry across 4,500 enterprise customers—corroborated by the latest Mandiant M-Trends report—global cyber incidents surged 68% year-over-year in Q3 alone. Ransomware remains the apex predator, accounting for 42% of breaches we mitigated, with average dwell times dropping to 11 days thanks to faster EDR adoption, but payouts climbing to $1.8 million per incident per IBM's Cost of a Data Breach study. What's new and concerning is the weaponization of generative AI: we've observed a 220% uptick in AI-generated phishing campaigns, including deepfake voice lures mimicking C-suite execs, which evaded 75% of legacy email gateways in our simulations.

Diving deeper into trends, supply chain compromises are the silent killer—up 145% from last year, echoing SolarWinds but now targeting third-party SaaS like Okta and Snowflake. In our MITRE ATT&CK coverage, we've mapped 92% of TTPs across the initial access and lateral movement tactics, with a spike in living-off-the-land binaries exploiting Windows native tools. Cloud-native threats are exploding too: misconfigurations in multi-cloud environments drove 81% of our cloud workload protection activations, per our CNAPP data, especially around Kubernetes RBAC flaws. And don't get me started on OT/IoT—ICS exploits rose 190% amid the push for Industry 4.0, with Modbus and DNP3 protocols in manufacturing being prime targets.

Regionally, it's a tale of three worlds. In North America, which represents 52% of our bookings, critical infrastructure resilience is paramount post-Colonial Pipeline and the Biden EO 14028 mandates. We've seen CISA alerts on Volt Typhoon actors targeting energy grids, driving 35% YoY growth in our OT security module. EMEA, at 28% of revenue, is GDPR-fueled paranoia: NIS2 Directive compliance has spiked demand for our zero-trust SASE platform by 51%, particularly in financial services where we've won displacements against Zscaler in three top-10 banks. APAC, our fastest-growing region at 19% of mix, faces geopolitical headwinds—Chinese APT41 variants and North Korean Lazarus Group have ramped up crypto heists, with Southeast Asia seeing a 310% jump in Magecart skimmers on e-commerce. Our Tokyo data center expansion is already yielding 40% attach rates for sovereign cloud workloads compliant with Japan's My Number Act.

Strategically, we're leaning into three pillars to outpace this. First, AI-native defense: our Nexus AI engine, now processing 10 trillion events daily with sub-50ms detection latency, uses unsupervised ML to hunt polymorphic malware that signature-based tools like legacy Symantec miss—resulting in 3.2x faster MTTR for customers. We've invested $450 million in FY24 R&D, including quantum-resistant post-quantum cryptography pilots with NIST's Kyber algorithm to future-proof against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. Second, ecosystem convergence: partnerships with Microsoft for Defender-XDR interoperability and AWS for native Bedrock integration have unlocked $300 million in co-sell pipeline. Third, managed services scale: our MSSP bookings hit $800 million TCV, with autonomous SOAR playbooks automating 65% of Level 1 triage.

The insight here? Attackers are democratizing destruction via commoditized tools like LockBit 3.0 leak sites and as-a-service models, but defenders win with platformization. Our customers using full-stack XDR + ZTNA see 94% breach prevention rates versus 62% for point solutions—validated in our latest Forrester TEI study showing 317% ROI over three years. Looking forward, we expect threat velocity to sustain 50-60% YoY growth through 2025, per Gartner’s forecast, amplifying our $18 billion TAM expansion into AI security and SMB verticals.

Sarah, does that address, or want me to unpack any regional specifics further?

Operator: Thank you. Next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Emily Rodriguez: Good afternoon. Excellent results once again. I'd love to hear more about customer feedback on your new products and features—how are they resonating?

Dr. Priya Singh: Thanks, Emily, and good afternoon, everyone. Before we move further, I'd like to dive deeper into one of the standout areas from our customer metrics: feedback on our new products and features. As you know, SecureNet has been aggressively innovating in the Zero Trust and XDR spaces to address the escalating threat landscape—think Log4Shell remnants, state-sponsored supply chain attacks like SolarWinds 2.0, and the 300% year-over-year surge in ransomware we've seen per our Threat Intelligence Report.

Overall, customer sentiment has been exceptionally strong. Our Net Promoter Score for new product releases hit 78 in Q2, up from 62 a year ago and well above the cybersecurity industry average of 55, as benchmarked by Gartner Peer Insights. Customer Satisfaction scores averaged 92% across beta and GA features, with 87% of surveyed customers reporting reduced mean time to detect and respond by an average of 45%. Renewal rates for bundles including our latest releases climbed to 98%, and we saw a 35% attach rate for upsells—that's customers adding features like our AI-driven behavioral analytics to existing EDR platforms.

Let me break this down by key product launches. First, our Cloud Native Application Protection Platform, which integrates CSPM and CWPP with real-time vulnerability prioritization using ML models trained on 10 trillion daily events. Feedback here has been phenomenal: 76% of early adopters—primarily Fortune 1000 enterprises in financial services—cited a 60% reduction in cloud misconfiguration risks, aligning with the 2024 Verizon DBIR findings on cloud breaches. One major bank in the US shared that our auto-remediation workflows blocked 1,200+ exploitable IaC flaws in their AWS multi-account environment pre-deployment. Adoption surged 52% quarter-over-quarter, with net new ARR from CNAPP at $28 million.

Next, the headline of Q2: SecureXDR 2.0, our unified Extended Detection and Response platform with native SOAR and GenAI threat hunting. This builds on our core EDR heritage, but with deeper integrations into SASE fabrics for hybrid workforces. Customers love the unified console—91% reported 30-50% faster triage times thanks to our natural language query interface, which leverages models fine-tuned on MITRE ATT&CK frameworks. In a blind A/B test with 150 beta users, SecureXDR outperformed legacy SIEMs like Splunk by 4x in false positive reduction, dropping from 15% to under 4%. We've secured 420 net new logos, including 12% from Zscaler's ecosystem partners, and early indicators show a 42% increase in multi-year contracts.

On the identity side, our Secure Identity Mesh feature set, with passwordless MFA and just-in-time access, garnered 95% CSAT. Feedback highlights seamless integration with ServiceNow for privileged access management, addressing the 81% of breaches tied to compromised credentials per IBM's Cost of a Data Breach Report. Uptake was strongest in regulated verticals, with 68% of healthcare customers adopting it post-Change Healthcare ransomware fallout.

Regionally, the story is equally compelling. In North America, which drove 62% of new product ARR, feedback emphasized ransomware resilience—our features thwarted 97% of LockBit variants in live simulations shared by USGBC members. EMEA saw 28% quarter-over-quarter growth, fueled by NIS2 compliance deadlines; German DAX firms praised our EU data sovereignty controls, with 82% reporting audit-ready posture improvements. APAC exploded 55% year-over-year, thanks to PDPA and APAC-specific threat intel on North Korean Lazarus campaigns—Singapore telcos and Japanese manufacturers cited 70% faster breach simulations via our platform.

Strategically, this feedback validates our 'Unified Threat Fabric' vision: converging endpoint, network, cloud, and identity under a single AI pane of glass. We're doubling down with $150 million in R&D for quantum-resistant crypto and edge AI inference, partnering with hyperscalers—AWS Marketplace listings up 40%, Azure co-sell deals yielding 22% of pipeline. Customer quotes from our 10-K underscore this: 'SecureNet's innovations cut our SOC headcount needs by 25% while boosting efficacy'—CTO, Global 200 retailer.

Looking ahead, we expect these trends to accelerate Q3 guidance: 25-28% year-over-year revenue growth, with new products contributing 45% of total ARR expansion. We're positioned to capture share in the $85 billion TAM, per IDC's 2024 forecast, as 72% of CISOs plan XDR consolidation per our Voice of the CISO survey.

Emily, happy to expand on any specific feature.

Operator: Thank you. Next question comes from David Kim with Barclays.

David Kim: Hi, team. Great quarter. Can you elaborate on average deal sizes for new and existing customers? Any regional or product insights?

Mark Thompson: Good afternoon, David, and thanks for the question. Happy to dive into a key metric that's been a bright spot in our performance: average deal size for new and existing customers. This continues to reflect the strength of our land-and-expand model in a cybersecurity landscape marked by escalating threats—like the 42% year-over-year surge in ransomware incidents reported by Chainalysis—and accelerating cloud migrations amid macroeconomic pressures.

First, on new customer average annual contract value, or ACV. In Q2, we achieved an average ACV of $478,000 for new logos, up 28% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit growth in new customer deal sizes. Driving this is our focus on mid-market and enterprise wins with our flagship XDR platform, Nexus Sentinel, which integrates AI-powered endpoint detection and response with our cloud-native SASE solution. For context, 62% of these deals included multi-product bundles—think Nexus Sentinel paired with our Zero Trust Network Access and Managed Detection and Response services—compared to just 41% a year ago.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, accounting for 68% of new logos with an average ACV of $525,000, fueled by hyperscaler partnerships like our expanded AWS Marketplace integration, which saw a 35% uptake in Q2. EMEA grew even faster at 45% year-over-year in deal size to $410,000, propelled by DORA compliance deadlines pushing financial institutions toward our EU-hosted sovereign cloud offerings. APAC lagged slightly at $395,000 but showed 22% quarter-over-quarter acceleration, thanks to wins in Japan and Australia amid rising state-sponsored APT campaigns, as highlighted in Mandiant's M-Trends report.

Shifting to existing customers, our average expansion ACV hit $682,000 in Q2—a robust 36% year-over-year increase and 15% quarter-over-quarter. This underscores our industry-leading net revenue retention of 128%, well above the 115-120% peer average for CrowdStrike and Zscaler. Expansions now represent 72% of our total ARR bookings, up from 65% last year, driven by cross-sell into high-velocity adjacencies like our AI SecOps platform, Sentinel AI, which automates threat hunting and response orchestration. Notable here: 55% of expansions involved upsizing to our full-stack Secure Access Service Edge suite, with average add-on ACV exceeding $250,000 per deal.

A quick regional lens: EMEA expansions averaged $710,000, boosted by GDPR fines averaging €4.5 million per breach, per IBM's Cost of a Data Breach report, prompting deeper Zero Trust adoptions. In APAC, we saw $645,000 averages amid PDPA and CCPA-like regulations, while North America held steady at $695,000 with Fortune 500 renewals bundling MDR for supply chain resilience post-Log4Shell echoes.

Overall, our blended average deal size—weighted by new and expansion mix—reached $612,000, a 32% year-over-year lift, contributing to 42% ARR growth to $1.8 billion. Strategically, this validates our 'platformization' bet: customers consolidating point solutions from legacy players like Symantec or Check Point into our unified SecureNet One platform, reducing their total cost of ownership by 30-40% while expanding our wallet share from 25% to 42% within 18 months of onboarding.

Looking forward, we expect Q3 new customer ACV to trend toward $500,000+ as we ramp GenAI security modules—addressing the 75% of organizations piloting LLMs per our SecureNet Threat Index—and Q4 expansions to benefit from our ecosystem plays with Microsoft Azure Sentinel integrations. This positions us to capture share in a $75 billion+ cybersecurity market growing at 14% CAGR, per Gartner.

David, anything else on this front?

Mark Thompson: Thank you, everyone, for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident that we can continue to deliver strong results.

Lisa Grant: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
